summary: Al2O3 and TiO2 thin films were deposited on various polymeric substrates such as PMMA, PEEK, PTFE, and ETFE using atomic layer deposition (ALD) at temperatures ranging from 80 to 250 /C176C. The films were studied for their growth rates, adhesion, and surface properties. The adhesion was good on PEEK but poor on PTFE. The water contact angles decreased on TiO2-coated surfaces under UV illumination, indicating superhydrophilic behavior.
evidence: Al2O3 and TiO2 thin films were deposited by atomic layer deposition at 80–250 /C176C on various polymeric substrates such as polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA), polyetheretherketone (PEEK), polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) and ethylenetetrafluoroethylene (ETFE). The adhesion of the films was good on PEEK and poor on PTFE. All coated surfaces showed lower water contact angles than the uncoated thermoplastics. Furthermore, the water contact angles on all TiO2-coated surfaces decreased upon UV illumination, most efficiently with crystalline TiO2 coatings.
